Incorporating the Beige Book for the May 2018 meeting: Districts reported modest-to-moderate growth, broad labor-market tightness, and wage gains in the modest-to-moderate range. Input and transportation costs (notably steel and trucking) were rising with some pass-through to final prices, consistent with inflation moving near 2%. Consumer spending was mixed with softer autos, while manufacturing and capex intentions remained solid but faced capacity constraints and trade-policy uncertainty. Credit conditions were generally accommodative with modestly stronger loan demand; standards were largely unchanged to slightly easier for C&I amid competition, while CRE standards tightened—aligning with the SLOOS.

Net, the Beige Book corroborates the FOMC’s “moderate” growth and strong labor conditions but adds caution via cost pressures, capacity constraints, and CRE softening. That tilts the tone slightly more cautious than a pure macro read while remaining moderately positive.
